text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Monday he had extended the deadline for an Austro-Italian consortium's bid for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt until midnight September 6.
The original deadline for the proposed bid by the consortium led by insurer EA-Generali and including savings bank Die Erste expired on Friday.
"I have met the consortium today and it asked for an extension. After consulting with our lawyers we have set this final deadline," Klima told reporters.
Klima said he would re-open the process and invite offers from other bidders if the extended deadline passed by without him receiving a final offer.
The minister said other potential bidders had contacted him, but he declined to give more details.

Die Erste Oesterreichische Spar-Casse Bank wants to set up a holding company with Creditanstalt-Bankverein, but talks with its partners, which also include Germany's Commerzbank were reported to have hit a snag.
Commerzbank over the weekend reportedly threatened to pull out of the consortium amid growing concern over the excessive weight Die Erste would carry in its proposed holding structure.
